The CODECO (container gate-in/gate-out report) message is used by a terminal, depot, etc. to confirm that specified containers have been delivered or picked up by the inland carrier (road, rail or barge) [1].

- **Gate activity reporting:** It reports gate movements of an item of equipment in and out of a container terminal, storage and repair facility, or packing/unpacking facility [2].
- **Internal movements:** It can report internal terminal container movements, but not loading or discharging the vessel [1]. It can also report movements within a facility, including changes to the equipment's status after servicing or repair [2].
- **Leasing industry:** It is also used to notify changes to a container's lease status, i.e. as a report of on/off hire or direct interchange [2].
- **Operational reports:** The message is intended for operational reports that may be used to update equipment tracking systems [2].

It is part of a set of container-related messages that facilitate intermodal handling of containers by streamlining information exchange [1].
rows.search_query: What is the CODECO message used for?
rows.reason: The answer states that a terminal or depot confirms delivery or pickup by inland carriers (road, rail or barge) as gate-in/gate-out, and that it can report internal movements excluding vessel loading/discharge, with no contradictions.

A COARRI (container discharge/loading report) is sent by the container terminal to report that specified containers have been discharged from a seagoing vessel (as ordered, overlanded or shortlanded) or loaded onto a seagoing vessel [1][4]. It is commonly sent by the terminal operator handling the vessel to the shipping line or its agent [1][3].

It may also be used to confirm that containers have been shifted on board the vessel, or that they have been discharged and reloaded (restowed) onto the vessel [3].

In the BGM segment, the document name code indicates the report type: 122 for a transport loading report, 119 for a transport discharge report, and 24 for a restow (used only to report the new stowage position) [5].
rows.search_query: What does a COARRI message report?
rows.reason: The answer states that the container terminal reports containers discharged from or loaded onto a seagoing vessel, matching the reference, and its additional details do not contradict it.

rows.answer:
The COPRAR message is commonly sent by the shipping line (or its agent) to the terminal operator handling the vessel [1].

It is an order telling the container terminal that the specified containers must be discharged from a seagoing vessel or loaded onto a seagoing vessel [1]. It may also be used to transmit details on containers that are to be shifted on board the vessel, or containers that are to be discharged and reloaded (restowed) onto the vessel [2].
rows.search_query: Who normally sends the COPRAR message and what does it instruct the terminal to do?
rows.reason: The answer says the shipping line or its agent sends COPRAR to the terminal, and that it orders the terminal to load or discharge containers on a seagoing vessel; the extra detail about shifting and restowing does not contradict the reference.

The COPINO (container pre-notification) message is used by an inland carrier to notify of the delivery or pick-up of containers [1][4]. It gives a facility advance notice that an item of transport equipment is to be delivered to that facility, or collected by an inland carrier at a specified time [1].

COPINO is part of a total set of container-related messages that serve to facilitate the intermodal handling of containers by streamlining the information exchange [1][4].
rows.search_query: What is the purpose of the COPINO message?
rows.reason: The answer covers every reference fact: an inland carrier gives advance notice to a facility that containers will be delivered or picked up, and nothing in it contradicts the reference.

rows.answer:
For vessels that allow 10 or more tiers on deck, on-deck tier numbering shall start with tier '72' instead of '82'. [1][2][4]

- **Why the change:** ISO 9711 defines tier numbers as 2-digit values, with on-deck tiers starting at "82" and rising in even numbers. That allows only nine tiers on deck (the 9th being "98"), so the scheme no longer works for vessels with 10 or more tiers. [1][3]
- **Goal:** Starting at '72' avoids three-digit tier numbers, which matters because many existing IT systems rely on 2-digit numeric tier numbers. [2][3]
- **Scope:** No change is intended for existing vessels. [1][2]
- **Origin:** SMDG approved this as Recommendation 01 in April 2013. [2]
- **In BAPLIE:** BAPLIE 3 refers to SMDG Recommendation #01, and the stowage location (7 digits, BBBRRTT) applies it for vessels allowing 10 or more tiers on deck. [4][5]
rows.search_query: How should on-deck tiers be numbered for vessels that can carry 10 or more tiers on deck?
rows.reason: The answer states that on-deck tier numbering starts at 72 instead of 82 to avoid three-digit tier numbers, matching all reference facts with nothing contradictory.

rows.answer:
If the container is marked with digits only and no letter prefix, the identification should still be transmitted exactly as marked on the box [1][3]. If a dummy prefix cannot be avoided for any reason, the only prefix to use is "NONE" [1][3]. "NONE" is meant solely to indicate that no prefix is present on the container [1], so SMDG recommends not marking it on any container [1].

- Do not add leading zeros or other digits to fill up to seven digits [1].
- Do not transmit whitespace or special characters such as '-', '/', '?' [5].
- At least one digit must be transmitted [1][5].
- In BAPLIE (EQD, data element C237.8260), the same rule applies: for numerals-only markings where a prefix cannot be avoided, NONE is prepended to the numerals [4]. The BAPLIE guide's example shows a container marked 9000122 and recommends transmitting it with the NONE prefix [4].
- If the equipment has no marking at all, BAPLIE says to send a unique sequence number prepended by NONE [4].
- A receiver should not expect the check-digit calculation to match when "NONE" is part of the identification [3].
rows.search_query: A container is marked only with digits and no letter prefix. How should its ID be sent in EDI?
rows.reason: The answer covers all three reference facts: transmit exactly as marked without padding, use 'NONE' only if a dummy prefix is unavoidable, and do not expect the check digit to match with NONE; the BAPLIE example could read as a general recommendation for NONE, but it sits under the stated 'cannot be avoided' condition, so it does not contradict the reference.

- **Full import containers → COREOR.** SMDG recommends COREOR for transmitting release instructions for FULL IMPORT containers only [1]. COREOR is defined as an order to release containers and permit pick-up by or on behalf of a specified party, and is used for release of full containers, either for export or for release to an importer or agent [4].

- **Export bookings and empty container release → COPARN.** SMDG recommends COPARN for transmitting EXPORT BOOKINGS, including the release instructions for EMPTY containers where applicable [1]. COPARN can also serve as an instruction to accept empty containers (Depot function) [1].

- **Note on COREOR and empties:** COREOR 2.0 says it may optionally be used to release empty transport equipment prior to packing [2], but the SMDG Recommendation 03 points to COREOR for full import containers only and COPARN for empty release [1].

An empty tank container with dangerous goods residue should be reported as follows:

- **Mark the equipment as Empty.** Where "empty" and "full" are denoted, as in the EQD segment, the container shall be marked as "empty" [2][3].
- **Use the attribute code ETR.** The SMDG Status Attribute Code "ETR" (Empty Tank with Residue) identifies the container as such, and carriers, terminals and customers may use it in all related EDIFACT messages [2][3].
- **Declare the hazardous properties in a Dangerous Goods declaration.** The container must be declared and reported as a DG container, and the same IMDG rules apply as for a DG container with cargo [1][2]. In messages such as COPRAR and COARRI this is done with the DGS segment (e.g. `DGS+IMD+3+2348+037:CEL+3+3-03'`), which identifies the UN number and class [5][6]. In IFTSTA, an FTX segment should be used at least once to give the dangerous goods technical name when DG is reported in the DGS segment [4].

The reason for this approach is that some IT systems automatically classify a container as "Full" when it has a DG property, which causes misunderstandings and extra email exchange. Marking it "empty" with ETR avoids this ambiguity [2][3].

The ETR code is published in the SMDG Attribute code list [3]. The excerpts do not specify which exact segment and qualifier carry the ETR code in each message type.
rows.search_query: How should an empty tank container that still has dangerous goods residue be reported in EDI?
rows.reason: The answer covers all three reference facts without contradicting any of them: mark the container as empty in EQD, use the SMDG attribute code ETR, and declare the hazardous properties with a DGS dangerous goods declaration.

The verified gross mass is carried in the **MEA segment** (segment 0180), which sits in segment group SG5 (MEA-DTM) [2].

**How it is structured**
- MEA is mandatory (M) with a maximum occurrence of 1 per group [2].
- The measurement purpose code qualifier (6311) is `AAE` = Measurement [2].
- The measured attribute code (6313) states the verification status: `VGM` = Transport equipment verified gross mass (weight), or `AET` = Transport equipment gross weight [2].
- If the gross mass is not yet determined or its verification status is not known, code `AET` must be transmitted [2].
- The unit code (6411) is `KGM` (kilogram) or `LBR` (pound), and the measure (6314) holds the value [5].
- Measurement significance code (6321), non-discrete measurement name code (6155) and non-discrete measurement name (6154) are not used [2][5].

**Examples**
- `MEA+AAE+VGM+KGM:21700'` (gross mass, verified) [5]
- `MEA+AAE+AET+KGM:20000'` (gross mass, not verified) [5]

**Optional date/time:** A DTM segment in the same group can give when the gross mass was determined, e.g. `DTM+798:202606251632:203'`, where 798 = verified gross mass determination date/time and 203 = CCYYMMDDHHMM [1][4].
rows.search_query: In VERMAS, which segment carries the verified gross mass, and what does it look like?
rows.reason: The answer names the MEA segment with qualifier AAE and code VGM and gives the example MEA+AAE+VGM+KGM:21700, and nothing in it contradicts the reference facts.

A container restow via the quay is reported as **two moves**: one for the discharge and one for the load [3]. The restow-reporting documentation repeats this, saying a restow via pier is always reported as 2 moves [4].

A restow with only one move onboard (a container shifted on the vessel) is counted separately under QTY 496 [1].

**Purpose:** TPFREP (Terminal Performance Report) is used to transmit information about operations carried out by terminal operators, such as the loading, discharging and re-stow of containers and hatch covers [1]. Terminal performance is in principle measured as "moves per hour" (per crane or per vessel, gross or net), and the message reports the basic data needed for this: the number of moves and the timestamps that delimit the underlying time periods [1]. Other terminal services (measuring, sealing, repairing, supervising, etc.) cannot be reported in TPFREP [1].

**Sender/receiver:** The message is transmitted by a terminal operator to the vessel operator [1]. The excerpt indicates it is also sent to someone "in addition," but the text is cut off, so I can't say to whom [1]. More broadly, the guide is intended for terminal operators, vessel operators, container operators, tonnage centres, etc. [6].

**Full vs. partial:** A "full" message (BGM code 265) contains all moves for all container operators, while "TPFREP light" (code 873) contains only the volumes for one carrier, not the total moves for the vessel [5]. Which one is used is agreed between terminal and carrier, but the message's original purpose is to enable meaningful key performance indicators, which only a "full" message can achieve [4].
rows.search_query: What is the TPFREP message for, and who sends it to whom?
rows.reason: The answer covers every reference fact: it reports terminal operations (loading, discharging, restows, hatch covers) with move counts and timestamps for moves-per-hour measurement, and it is sent by the terminal operator to the vessel operator, with no contradictions.

**What MOVINS is used for**
- MOVINS is the EDIFACT stowage instruction message. It transmits information about all activities such as discharging, shifting, restowing and loading on a specified means of transport. [1]
- It goes from the operator or owner of the means of transport (or a stowage centre) to any party involved in the operation, e.g. the terminal operator. [1][4]
- Complete MOVINS messages are normally sent, but EDI partners may agree on partial messages, e.g. Discharge only, followed by Loading, Restow and Shift. [1]
- SMDG recommends MOVINS mainly for restow/shifting instructions and for the stowage position when loading boxes. [3]
- The instructions apply to the data in the terminal's planning system, which should already know the vessel details (bays, rows/tiers under and on deck). [1]

**Relation to BAPLIE**
- Information in a MOVINS message generally applies to data previously received in a BAPLIE message. [4]
- The results of the operation can optionally be reflected in a new BAPLIE message. [4]
- The MOVINS structure is based on BAPLIE, and the sequence of related segments (DTM, RFF, NAD, followed by TDT/LOC/DTM of group 1) is the same as in BAPLIE. [4]
- The receiver can therefore extract information from MOVINS and use it to build a new BAPLIE bayplan. [4]
- BAPLIE itself is used before vessel arrival to provide the previous port's vessel stowage plan. [3]
rows.search_query: What is MOVINS used for and how does it relate to BAPLIE?
rows.reason: The answer covers all three reference facts: MOVINS carries stowage instructions (discharge, shift, restow, load) from the vessel operator or stowage centre to the terminal, it applies to data previously received in a BAPLIE, and the result may be reflected in a new BAPLIE, with nothing contradicting them.

DESTIM (Equipment Damage and Repair Estimate) is a message for the container repair, shipping and leasing industry [2].

- **From depot to owner/user:** A container repair depot can use it to send an owner or user a description of the damage to the equipment, together with an estimate of the repair actions and costs needed to fix it [2].
- **Forwarding to a lessee:** A recipient owner may forward the estimate on to a lessee [2].
- **Authorization and acknowledgment:** An owner or lessee can use the message to authorize the repair depot to perform the repairs listed in the estimate, and to acknowledge that they are willing to pay for the repairs indicated for their account [2].

The message type code in the UNH segment is DESTIM, in version D, release 96B [1][5].
rows.search_query: What is the DESTIM message used for?
rows.reason: The answer covers both reference facts: the repair depot sends the owner/user a damage description with an estimate of repair actions and costs, and the message can be used to authorize the repairs, with no contradictions.

VGM(검증된 총중량)은 **MEA 세그먼트**로 보냅니다.

- MEA 세그먼트는 운송 장비(컨테이너)의 총중량을 지정하고, 그 중량이 SOLAS 규정 등에 따라 검증되었는지 여부를 표시하는 용도입니다. [4]
- 검증된 총중량 예시: `MEA+AAE+VGM+KGM:21700'` (검증된 총중량) [4]
- 검증되지 않은 총중량 예시: `MEA+AAE+AET+KGM:20000'` [4]
- 단위 코드(6411)는 KGM(킬로그램) 또는 LBR(파운드)을 사용할 수 있으며, 중량 값은 6314(Measure)에 넣습니다. [4]

참고로, 총중량이 측정된 일시는 별도로 DTM 세그먼트(예: `DTM+798:202606251632:203'`)로 전달할 수 있습니다. 이는 총중량을 둘 이상 전송하거나 VGM을 재측정한 경우 최신 버전을 식별하는 데 선택적으로 사용됩니다. [1]

갑판 위 10단 이상을 허용하는 컨테이너선은 갑판 위(on-deck) 티어 번호를 '72'부터 시작합니다. 세 자리 티어 번호가 생기는 것을 피하기 위한 규칙입니다. [1][2][3][4]

배경과 세부 사항은 다음과 같습니다.
- ISO 9711은 티어 번호를 두 자리 숫자로 정하고, 갑판 위 티어는 "82"부터 짝수로 증가하도록 규정합니다. 이 규칙으로는 갑판 위 9단("98")까지만 표현할 수 있습니다. [2]
- 기존 IT 시스템 대부분이 두 자리 숫자 티어 번호에 의존하고 규칙 변경에 큰 비용이 들기 때문에, SMDG는 2013년 4월에 이 권고안을 승인했습니다. [3]
- 기존 선박에는 변경이 없습니다. [1][3]
- 본선 적재 위치(stowage location)는 BBBRRTT 형식의 정확히 7자리로 전송하며, 10단 이상 선박에는 이 티어 번호 권고를 적용합니다. [5]
- BAPLIE 3도 갑판 위 10단 이상에 대해 SMDG 권고 #01을 참조합니다. [4]

문서에 나온 내용은 시작 번호가 '72'라는 것까지이며, 그 이후 번호가 어떻게 이어지는지(예: 72, 74, 76…)는 발췌문에 명시되어 있지 않습니다.

rows.reason: The answer says on-deck tiers start at 72 instead of the usual 82, which matches the reference fact, and none of the extra details contradict it.

BAPLIE 버전 2가 2007년에 도입된 이후 다음 분야에서 기능 개선이 필요해졌기 때문입니다 [1]:

- 위험물(DG) 설명에 더 많은 세부 정보 필요 [1]
- 비표준 장비, 빈 플랫랙(flat rack), 번들, 브레이크벌크(breakbulk) 처리 [1]
- 회계 상세 정보: 파트너 선사 간 슬롯 공유, 손실 슬롯 [1]
- 안전 검증용 데이터: 중량 한계, 중량 분포, DG 적재 및 격리 [1]

버전 3의 구조적 개선점은 다음과 같습니다.
- 적재 위치(stowage location)를 정보의 기준(anchor)으로 유지하고, 장비 세부 정보는 EQD 그룹에서 더 상세히 지정합니다 [6].
- 위험물 데이터 범위를 확장합니다 [6]. 새 DGS 그룹으로 IMDG Code에 따라 DG 품목을 완전히 식별하며, LQ(Limited Quantities)와 CFR49 화물 같은 특수 사례도 다룹니다 [2].
- 취급 지시를 코드로 구조화하고, 모든 데이터를 구조화된 요소에 담아 자유 텍스트 우회 방식을 없앴습니다 [6].
- 전송 가능한 적재 위치의 최대 수가 9999에서 99999로 늘었습니다 [2].

기대 효과는 다음과 같습니다 [4].
- 구조화된 정보 덕분에 터미널 작업 중단 감소

rows.answer:
CODECO(Container Gate-in/Gate-out Report) 메시지는 주로 컨테이너의 게이트 활동을 보고합니다.

- **공식 정의**: 터미널, 데포 등이 지정된 컨테이너가 내륙 운송업체(도로, 철도, 바지선)에 의해 인도되었거나 반출되었음을 확인하는 메시지입니다. [2]
- **게이트 활동 보고**: 컨테이너 터미널, 보관·수리 시설, 적입/적출(packing/unpacking) 시설을 드나드는 장비(equipment)의 게이트 이동을 보고하기 위한 것입니다. [3]
- **시설 내부 이동**: 터미널 내부의 컨테이너 이동(본선 적하·양하는 제외)과, 서비스나 수리 후 장비 상태 변경도 보고할 수 있습니다. [2][3]
- **리스 업계 용도**: 컨테이너 리스 상태의 변경, 즉 on/off hire 또는 direct interchange의 통지에도 사용됩니다. [3]
- **VGM 관련 사용 사례**: 계량 시설이 운송 장비의 검증 총중량(Verified Gross Mass) 측정 결과를 주문 고객(화주 또는 포워더)에게 회신하는 용도로도 쓰일 수 있습니다. [5]
- **목적**: 운영 보고서를 제공하는 메시지이며, 장비 추적 시스템을 갱신하는 데 활용될 수 있습니다. [3]

수입 적컨테이너(FULL IMPORT container)의 반출 지시에는 **COREOR(Container Release Order)** 메시지를 사용해야 합니다.

- SMDG Recommendation #3은 선사 또는 그 대리점이 터미널로 보내는 메시지 중, FULL IMPORT 컨테이너의 반출(release) 지시에는 COREOR만 사용할 것을 권장합니다. [1]
- COREOR는 컨테이너의 반출을 지시하고, 지정된 당사자(또는 그 대리인)가 컨테이너를 픽업할 수 있도록 허가하는 메시지입니다. [3]
- COREOR는 수출용 또는 수입자/대리점에 대한 반출 등 적컨테이너(full container)의 반출에 사용됩니다. [3]

참고로, COPARN은 수출 부킹(EXPORT BOOKINGS)과 해당되는 경우 공컨테이너(EMPTY)의 반출 지시에 사용하도록 권장되므로, 수입 적컨테이너 반출용이 아닙니다. [1]

컨테이너 식별 번호는 EDI 메시지에서 컨테이너에 표시된 그대로 전송하는 것이 원칙입니다 [1][3].

숫자로만 되어 있는 경우의 처리 방법은 다음과 같습니다.

- 어떤 이유로든 더미 접두어(prefix)를 피할 수 없다면, 컨테이너 자체에 접두어가 없음을 나타내기 위해 'NONE'을 사용할 것을 강력히 권장합니다 [3].
- 'NONE'은 EDI 전송에서 "컨테이너에 접두어가 없음"을 표시하는 용도로만 사용해야 하며, 컨테이너에 실제 마킹으로 사용하지 않을 것을 권장합니다 [1].
- 접두어 없이 더미 접두어가 불가피할 때는 'NONE' 외의 다른 접두어를 전송해서는 안 됩니다 [1].
- 숫자가 7자리 미만이더라도 앞에 0이나 다른 숫자를 채워 넣어서는 안 됩니다 [1].
- BAPLIE에서는 EQD의 C237.8260 데이터 요소에 식별번호를 가급적 장비에 표시된 그대로 전송하되, 숫자만 있고 (더미) 접두어를 피할 수 없으면 숫자 앞에 NONE을 붙이도록 합니다 [5]. 마킹이 전혀 없는 경우에는 NONE을 앞에 붙인 고유 일련번호를 전송합니다 [5].
- 수신 측에서 식별번호에 'NONE'이 포함되어 있다면 체크섬(check sum) 계산이 일치하지 않을 수 있으며, 이를 기대해서는 안 됩니다 [3].
